newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-GERMANY'S SEIZINGER FASTEST IN TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GERMANY'S SEIZINGER FASTEST IN TRAINING.

text.p: Germany's Katja Seizinger appeared to have rediscovered her form at the Alpine skiing world championships on Monday by posting the fastest time in the women's first downhill training.

After sustaining concussion in a crash at a World Cup downhill in Laax eight days ago and a disappointing sixth place at Sunday's championship giant slalom, Seizinger surprised even herself with a quickest time of one minute 41.94 seconds.
"It's unusual for me to have the quickest training time," said Seizinger, the 1994 Olympic downhill champion and last year's world championship silver medalist.
But while Seizinger has evidently recovered, Sweden's runaway leader in overall World Cup standings Pernilla Wiberg has flu and following the training session said: "I should be in bed."
Wiberg's goals this winter are the downhill and super-G gold medals -- the only titles missing from the double Olympic and three-time world champion's illustrious collection.
The 26-year-old Swede has never won a World Cup downhill but finished third at the season's first race in Lake Louise.
Seizinger, the overall World Cup title-holder, won in Lake Louise in November, finished second a week later in Vail, but failed to make the discipline's podium since then.
"These were my type of conditions today. The piste was not as icy as it had been for the men," she said. "But times from the first training run mean nothing at all."

After the men's competition last Saturday, organiser's flattened most of the jumps on the Kandahar-Banchetta piste and removed the ice from the Aqua Minerale corner -- which had claimed Austrian favourites Werner Franz and Josef Strobl.
"The slope is great. The jumps could be a bit longer but I'm not complaiming. I just hope the snow becomes more compact for our race (on Saturday).
"I rate this slope among the top downhill slopes -- like Lillehammer, Morzine and Cortina," said Seizinger.
Swiss favourite Heidi Zurbriggen, winner of two World Cup downhills this season, clocked the ninth fastest time of 1:44.30 and disagreed with Seizinger.
"I think the course could be tougher. It is virtually impossible to make mistakes in the top and bottom sections and the middle is very flat," she said.
"It's not as demanding as Cortina and Laax. I hope it becomes icier again."
Local Italian heroine Isolde Kostner, who tied for downhill victory with Zurbriggen in Cortina, posted the third best practice time of 1:43.23, behind Austria's Stefanie Schuster.
Kostner, the 1994 Olympic bronze medalist, said compatriot Deborah Compagnoni had removed the pressure from the Italian team with her two championship golds last week.
"We are all a lot more calm after Deborah's victories," said Kostner. "But she did her part, now we want to continue on the same lines."
Missing from Saturday's race will be defending champion Picabo Street. The American is still nursing a knee injury sustained during a downhill training crash before the season's opening race.
